newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rasselstein Hoesch sees more 96/97 tinplate sales.
newsitem.headline: Rasselstein Hoesch sees more 96/97 tinplate sales.

text.p: German tinplate producer Rasselstein Hoesch GmbH said it was expecting sales to rise to 1.2 million tonnes in the 1996/97 year (ending September 30) from 1.1 million in 1995/96.

A statement from the produder-funded tinplate promotion agency IZW said orders for the first half of 1997 were high and Rasselstein Hoesch's two plants at Andernach and Dortmund were operating at full capacity.
Domestic demand was robust and producer and consumer stocks were empty, board member Jost Massenberg was quoted as saying.
Export sales would benefit from the lower mark versus sterling and the dollar, but profits would lag the expected increase in sales due to cost pressures.
Massenberg said some major consumers -- canstock makers which supply the drinks industry -- might shift capacity back from Britain to Germany due to high sterling.
Rasselstein Hoesch sales of 1.1 million tonnes in 1995/96 were up from 917,000 in 1994/95.
Of the total, 980,000 tonnes were tin-bearing and chrome-coated steel (ECCS) and 139,000 tonnes so-called black steel, thin material without coating, used for example for interior building work.
Sales in Germany amounted to 500,000 tonnes, off four percent, while sales to EU countries rose by 1.5 percent to 212,000 tonnes and overseas exports jumped 22 percent to 407,000.
Rasselstein, which has a 20 percent market share in Europe and is the world's leading exporter, merged its operations with the only other German producer, Krupp Hoesch Stahl AG, in July 1995.
